defects: Introduces an arbitrary, unconstrained measure μ instead of the fixed Lebesgue/volume measure implicit in the gold statement; without tying μ to volume the theorem is false (e.g. μ = 0 gives RHS = 0 while LHS can be positive)

Wrong summation indexing: sums f(k) for k = 0,...,n-1 (includes f(0)) instead of f(k+1) for the corresponding range (starts at f(1)); this reverses which Riemann-sum bound applies and makes the inequality false in general even under Lebesgue measure (counterexample: f(x)=1/(x+1)^2, whose sum from k=0 exceeds its integral over [0,∞))
Fixes the starting point a = 0 (Set.Ici 0) instead of allowing a general a : ℕ as in the gold statement
Requires AntitoneOn f on the entire ray Ici 0 rather than only on the finite interval Icc a b, a stronger hypothesis than gold's per-(a,b) requirement
Uses HasFiniteIntegral alone instead of IntegrableOn, omitting the AEStronglyMeasurable component that IntegrableOn bundles
